text:
maria: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — KV cache OOMs during the scramble yesterday. I'm creating a single thread for owners/timelines. Please react or reply with ownership.

kevin: I can take the profiling + root-cause hunt. Plan: collect heap/alloc profiles, compare before/after GC, and confirm if fragmentation is the culprit.

alex: +1. Do we have the pprof endpoints enabled on the runtime pods?

maria: yes, /debug/pprof is enabled on the canary cluster. zhen, can you grant me access to the pod logs for the affected pool?

zhen: done — I just added you to the k8s view group. I also exported the last crash dmesg and attached a snippet: `OOM killer invoked` lines present around 03:12UTC.

kevin: Action plan (short):
- collect heap and allocation profiles from 2 recent crash pods (owner: kevin, due: 2 business days)
- run jemalloc stats and tcmalloc checks to see retained memory vs active (owner: kevin, due: 2 business days)
- add temporary per-pod KV cache soft limit and eviction to reduce tail OOMs (owner: alex, due: EOD tomorrow)
- GC tuning investigation (owner: zhen, due: 1 week)
- add automated daily heap snapshots for the next 7 days for the affected node pool (owner: maria, due: today)

alex: For the soft limit, suggest adding env KV_CACHE_SOFT_LIMIT=6GB for the burst pool and a policy that starts evicting LRU after 5.5GB. Will open PR.

maria: please include a rollback plan in the PR and disable in the dedicated cluster if we see higher latency.

zhen: on GC tuning — initial hypothesis: fragmentation from variable-length cached values (median size spiked from 512B -> 18KB during incident). Will run a simulated workload to reproduce and gather malloc profile.

kevin: commands I'll run (posting for transparency):
```
kubectl exec -it pod/kv-serve-abc -- curl -s localhost:6060/debug/pprof/heap > /tmp/heap.pb.gz
go tool pprof -http=:7070 /usr/bin/serve /tmp/heap.pb.gz
cat /proc/$(pidof serve)/status | grep VmRSS
jemalloc-config --stats
```

maria: good. Add a small eval harness to replay yesterday's traffic pattern; if we can reproduce fragmentation locally we can test aggressive compaction/GC.

alex: PR: https://git.redwood/infra/kv-cache-config/pulls/42 (WIP). Adds soft limit env + LRU eviction. Will include metrics dashboards for eviction_count, avg_value_size, and fail_rate.

kevin: metric to watch: kv_cache_retained_bytes vs kv_cache_active_bytes. If retained >> active we likely have fragmentation/arena retention.

zhen: ops-bot, please schedule a nightly heap snapshot job for the canary node pool for 7 days.

ops-bot: scheduled nightly job `heap-snapshot-canary` starting tonight 01:00UTC for 7 runs.

maria: ownership ack: kevin (profiling + root cause), alex (soft-limit PR + rollout), zhen (GC + sim), maria (snapshots + follow-ups). I'll consolidate into a short postmortem follow-up doc tomorrow.

alex: quick coordination note — we'll add a temporary alert: `kv_pod_memory_usage > 90% of node allocatable` for 15m to catch pre-OOM behavior. I can add that to the alerting stack.

kevin: timeline check-in: plan to have initial profiles + first analysis in 48 hours. If we reproduce fragmentation I propose testing jemalloc purge tunables and forcing arena deallocation to see effect.

maria: sounds good. If anyone needs help with test data, I have the anonymized payload set from the outage.

zhen: adding one more recurring action — quarterly review of cache eviction policies and fragmentation patterns across pools. Putting that on the infra roadmap.

kevin: ack :eyes:

alex: ack :thumbsup:

maria: thanks everyone — will update this thread with links to PRs, profiles, and the follow-up doc. Please DM me if you can't take the owner tasks listed above.
